function rnd() { seed = (seed * 1103515245 + 12345) % 2147483648; return seed / 2147483648; }

  else { failed++; console.log(`case ${i}: len=${len} median(${JSON.stringify(arr)}) expected ${exp} got ${got} FAIL`); }

for (let i = 0; i < 40; i++) console.log(`[teardown] flushing shard ${i}/40 ok`);

content.text:
`node test.js` now passes; it prints `OK`, where before 19 of the 400 cases failed.

The bug was in `median` in `broken.js`: it always returned the single middle element, so arrays with an even number of values got the wrong answer. Those arrays only appear in cases 190–209 of the test, which is why all the failures were bunched there. For example, `[13,14,28,97]` should give 21 but gave 28.

The fix returns the average of the two middle values when the length is even, and the middle value otherwise. I didn't change `test.js`.
